extracted.intended_audience: acousticians, experimental physicists, instrument designers, and scientific readers of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, calibrating, and using an absolute phonometer/phone to measure sound intensity and related acoustical quantities (e.g., ground reflection) with instrumentation and experimental protocols described. Includes source design, receiver design, tuning, calibration, and measurement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute measurement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The instrument should give indications in absolute measure — units that do not depend on time, place, or the instrument so another instrument built from the specifications would reproduce the same sound measures later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the source and receiver so units are reproducible and independent of observer or apparatus; document specifications so measurements can be replicated in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a pure tone as standard source
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard source of sound should emit a pure tone (sinusoid) analogous to a tuning-fork so the pressure waveform is a simple harmonic function of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a pure-tone source to simplify measurement and analysis; relate measurements to a well-defined sinusoidal standard to enable absolute comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiver sensitivity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiver (phonometer) must be extremely sensitive because sound pressure variations are only a few millionths of an atmosphere even for loud voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extremely sensitive detection (optical interferometry or high-magnification optical readout) and minimize damping and noise to detect minute pressure changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of reflections / free-field approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurements in enclosed spaces are influenced by reflections; to approximate free-field measurements one should remove reflecting objects or use a known reflecting plane (e.g., level ground) whose reflection coefficient can be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either measure far from reflecting surfaces (ideally infinite distance) or perform controlled experiments with a single reflecting plane of known reflection coefficient (e.g., golf course ground) and account for reflections in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diaphragm design for the phonometer
rubrics_metrics.description: The diaphragm should be effectively free (not performing work), carry a small plane mirror at its center, and be observed optically (fringes or interferometer) so the diaphragm motion is detected without mechanical loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a thin plate or disc (mica or aluminium) supported to minimize damping; affix a mirror for optical detection; avoid designs that impose significant mechanical work on the diaphragm (e.g., heavy coupling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical interferometric detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use optical interferometry (e.g., Michelson) or Newton’s rings/fringes to detect diaphragm motion, which overcomes alignment and contact problems and yields very high sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a Michelson interferometer to avoid the lens hitting a vibrating mirror and to permit large mirror separation; interferometer can be used for calibration even if practical measurements use a different optical readout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-degree-of-freedom resonant tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance sensitivity by using resonance twice: a tuned diaphragm (plate) plus a tuned resonator (back cavity), forming a coupled two-degree-of-freedom system whose tuning properties magnify the incident sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the system with 'mistuning' coordinates for plate and resonator; choose mistunings of the same sign and appropriate magnitude based on damping coefficients rather than tuning both to zero; treat the system mathematically like a wireless receiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize damping to maximize sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimate sensitiveness depends on the smallness of the damping of the plate (and resonator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design supports, openings, and resonator geometry to reduce acoustic and structural damping; prefer suspensions and construction that limit energy loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration protocol using interferometer
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate diaphragm motion with an interferometer; thereafter record movements using a torsion strip and mirror/telescope arrangement for operational measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interferometer for initial calibration to establish absolute scale, then use high-magnification optical projection (1200–1500×) of a mirror-mounted filament image for routine readings to match interferometer sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous and practical tuning mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a continuous tuning mechanism for the diaphragm/resonator (e.g., tensioned disc supported by three wires and micrometer-controlled pegs) rather than discrete mass additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace mass-adding tuning with adjustable tension or other continuous adjustments to enable tunability over broad ranges (two octaves or more) and to reduce damping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of the sound source (phone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The source (phone) can be a reversed phonometer: a tuned disc driven by alternating current via electromagnets and measured by microscope so emission is known in absolute measure; drive schemes such as a triode valve oscillator can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a tunable driven diaphragm with precise control (e.g., triode valve excitation), and measure its mechanical excursion optically to quantify emitted sound in absolute units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground reflection coefficient measurement method
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the coefficient of reflection of the ground by fixing phone and phonometer heights, moving one horizontally at constant height, reading varying phonometer deflections, and identifying interference minima from direct and reflected sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform scans along a line at constant height; observe interference minima with ear or instrument; grass/gravel found ~95% reflective; ensure windless conditions for best accuracy (~2% overall).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of resonance and mistuning graph for system tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent diaphragm and resonator tuning in a graph where coordinates are mistunings; optimal tuning is not centered (both zero) but both mistunings should share sign and magnitude according to damping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot and use theoretical/mathematical analysis (analogous to wireless receiver theory) to select tuning points that maximize sensitivity given system damping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace diaphragm with rigid disc on tensioned wires to reduce damping
rubrics_metrics.description: A rigid disc supported by tensioned steel wires and adjustable clamps reduces damping compared to previous diaphragms and increases sensitivity greatly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a spider clamp with three wires and micrometer adjustment to regulate tension; place disc in annular opening of resonator to minimize damping and extend tunable range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical optical readout for routine measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Record diaphragm movement with a thin steel torsion strip carrying a concave mirror and a magnified image of a straight filament seen through a telescope for practical high-sensitivity readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use magnifications of ~1200–1500× to approach interferometer sensitivity for routine measurements; ensure stable optical alignment and minimize mechanical vibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements: use mica diaphragm and white-light fringes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a thin mica plate for the diaphragm and employing fringes in white light allow high sensitivity and use of ordinary light sources (gas, incandescent, arc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mica diaphragms where appropriate and exploit white-light interference fringes to simplify illumination requirements in optical detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity demonstration and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate instrument sensitivity by projecting colored interference fringes and observing their disappearance when a faint distant sound is produced; verify ability to detect tuning-fork sounds barely audible to the ear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative demonstrations (fringe disappearance) and quantitative calibration checks against known faint sources to validate sensitivity claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications and functional criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrument should be applicable to a variety of acoustical experiments: measuring transmission through fabrics/walls/telephone booths, exploring fields within horns/tubes, maritime/navigation uses (direction finding phonotrope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design attachments (tubes, antennas, twin-horn assemblies) and portability to service multiple experimental and practical applications; validate each application with targeted tests (e.g., direction accuracy to within a few degrees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample selection for historical/biographical statistical study
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing seasonal incidence of births among eminent people, collect a list (here >200) focused on the relevant population (creative intellects, musicians, scientists, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose sample composition deliberately (define 'eminent' and included professions); be explicit about selection criteria to avoid bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative baseline for distribution analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observed birth-date distributions against an appropriate baseline (e.g., Registrar General’s average returns over a representative period) to determine correspondence or deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-period averaged baseline data (example: 12-year average) to contextualize observed distributions and test for non-random patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping/time-window analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze seasonal patterns by grouping months into meaningful windows (e.g., three-month quarters such as December–February) to reveal seasonal peaks or troughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate counts into quarter-year groups or other windows to highlight trends; report both month-by-month and grouped summaries for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locomotive performance specification (as an engineering evaluation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: For electric locomotive design evaluate by intended role (shunting, freight, passenger) and by quantitative performance goals (e.g., haul 450 tons, start on specified gradient within set distance/time, attain 65 mph, safe operation at 90 mph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define operational scenario and required performance metrics; compare proposed designs against these quantified targets and consider standardization constraints for passenger vs. freight/shunting designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbo-compressor material and operating limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Turbo-compressor design must tolerate extremely high rotational speeds and temperatures (e.g., up to 53,000 rpm, peripheral tip speeds ~670 m/s, stresses equivalent to very large centrifugal forces, operating temperatures 650–750°C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select materials and cooling schemes that handle centrifugal stresses and high-temperature operation; account for unusual demands on material strength and thermal resistance in design evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental nozzle flow methodology for supersaturation hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate greater-than-theoretical discharge through nozzles by assuming partial supersaturation of steam; use search tubes in nozzles to measure pressure drop and compare discharge with theory to assess supersaturation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to measure local pressure distributions along the nozzle, plot discharge vs. superheat, and compare forms of flow curves against predictions from complete-supersaturation assumptions; recognize limitations of obtaining Wilson-effect conditions in nozzles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established theoretical frameworks for instrument and phenomenon analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply existing mathematical and physical theories (e.g., Helmholtz, Rayleigh, Euler, Horn theory) to model instruments and acoustic phenomena such as musical instruments and resonators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage established theoretical work to guide apparatus design and interpret results; extend or adapt approximate theories (e.g., horn theory) when they show practical agreement with experiments.
